name: APA Hotel Keisei Ueno Ekimae Minami
detail: It was a very satisfying stay during this trip to Tokyo. Above all, the staff were friendly, and being able to receive assistance in Korean made the check-in and usage process very convenient. I was even more satisfied as there were almost no inconveniences due to language during my overseas travel. The breakfast was also better than expected. I was satisfied with both the variety and taste of the food, and it was nice to have a hearty breakfast before starting my day of travel. The location was convenient for sightseeing and moving around from Ueno, and overall, I could stay clean and comfortably. I was very satisfied with this stay and would like to use this hotel again when I visit Tokyo next time. Thank you for providing friendly service and a great accommodation experience.

name: The Millennials Shibuya
detail: This was a place I was really satisfied with during my stay in Shibuya. At first, I was a bit worried about noise and discomfort since it was a capsule hotel, but I felt completely comfortable, which made those worries irrelevant. The best part was the sleeping environment. I hardly noticed any surrounding noise, and the bed was much larger and more comfortable than I expected, making it great for relieving the fatigue accumulated during travel. The bedding was neatly maintained, and the personal space was well divided, allowing me to rest without worrying about privacy. The shower room and common areas were also very clean. I continuously felt that the facilities were well managed, and I didn't encounter any discomfort during my stay. Its location was central in Shibuya, making it easy to move around, and there were many convenience stores and restaurants nearby, making it a great spot for traveling. Above all, the staff's response was truly kind. From check-in to my stay, whenever I asked questions, they provided friendly and quick guidance, allowing me to have a pleasant stay. I was satisfied with the price, location, facilities, and service, and if I visit Shibuya again, I would want to return to this accommodation without a doubt. I believe it’s a place that would satisfy even those who have preconceived notions about capsule hotels.

name: APA Hotel Shinjuku-Kabukicho Tower
detail: The location requires a bit of a walk from Shinjuku Station, but it's nice because there are places to eat and shop nearby. On the way to the accommodation, I often saw cats on the LED screen, and while waiting for the elevator in the lodging, I could see Godzilla's back. It was great to use the large public bath for free every day. When I checked in on the first day, after a little past two in the afternoon, I left my luggage and planned to check in later, but a staff member who could speak Korean kindly helped me check in early, which was the best~🙆🏻‍♂️ The accommodation is small, but considering the price, it was excellent👍🏻 The surrounding area is a hot spot for young Japanese friends, so there was some noise from people drinking all night, which was a downside. There were events, like food trucks and different performances every evening right in front of the hotel, which was nice to see, but the noise from outside was directly audible in the room. There didn't seem to be noise coming from other rooms, possibly due to the noise from outside. I'm not sensitive to noise, so my overall satisfaction was high. If I travel to Tokyo again, I plan to stay here again. I went during Chuseok, and Japan also has holidays, so please take that into consideration when reading this review~~

name: Shinagawa Prince Hotel East Tower
detail: The Shinagawa Prince Hotel was a place where I used to make reservations for people on business trips when I worked in the General Affairs Department a long time ago. This time, I stayed there for the first time myself, and I felt quite emotional about it. Looking at the room size beforehand, I thought it might be small, but when I entered, it felt very functional, with everything neatly and compactly arranged. There was no sense of claustrophobia, and it was very comfortable. Additionally, on the second floor of the Annex building, there was a food court starting at 1400 yen, so even though it was a hotel, I was able to eat what I liked at a reasonable price, which was great. It was open until 10 PM. There was also a convenience store nearby. The bathtub showed signs of aging, as it felt a bit dirty at the bottom, but like in other hotels, it didn't bother me too much. It was just one night, but it was great to be able to stay close to the station at a good price.

name: APA Hotel Higashi Shinjuku Kabukicho Tower
detail: As it was my first trip to Tokyo, I was quite worried, but after carefully considering one of the three hotels recommended by a friend living in Tokyo, I found this place located in Shinjuku on Agoda and decided to book it a month in advance because there was a promotion sale, allowing me to reserve at a discounted price and pay for the accommodation early. After booking the flight tickets and the accommodation, the Japan trip started to feel real. I arrived at the hotel around 8 PM and checked in, where the staff kindly assisted me. My room was on the 10th floor, which was great as it was right in the middle of a building that had over 20 floors. The room was small but had everything I needed and was clean. I arrived on a Sunday and stayed for four nights until Thursday; I didn’t request breakfast separately, but I thought I should try it at least once, so I had the hotel breakfast on Tuesday morning in the cafeteria on the first floor. The chef was cooking directly, and there was a variety of delicious food, including fruits, vegetables, beverages, and meats, and I had a really satisfying meal. The cleaning system was set for every three days, but bathroom towels and various items could be replaced daily, and there were washers and dryers on the second floor, so I did laundry on Tuesday evening. There was also a large public bath, but I preferred showering in my room, so I didn’t use the public bath. If I visit Tokyo again, I would likely stay at this hotel again. The staff were very kind, and it was close to various subway stations, making transportation very convenient and pleasant. Above all, it felt safe, which made it a 100% satisfying experience for me as a woman traveling alone. Thank you so much to the staff. Wishing you all good health and happiness!

name: APA Hotel Roppongi SIX
detail: The interior is clean, and there is a bus stop right in front and an underground passage to the station, making it a great location even on rainy days! The staff was also accommodating and took care of my luggage before check-in, allowing me to have a comfortable stay! The amenities are abundant as well.👌´-

name: APA Hotel ＆ Resort Nishishinjuku Gochome Ekimae Tower
detail: The room is small, but that's typical for Japanese business hotels. The staff are very friendly. There is a bath, which is perfect for relieving work fatigue and wrapping up the day. On the second floor, there is a bathroom and a laundromat, as well as an unmanned convenience store, making it convenient. There are many 24-hour convenience stores nearby and two restaurants that are open 24 hours or until dawn, which I mostly use. The subway station is close, and it has good accessibility to other stations while the accommodation itself is quiet, making it nice. I started staying here on a recommendation during my first business trip, and I'm still using the same accommodation up to my fifth trip. The bed and bedding are also soft and nice.

name: WPÜ HOTEL SHINJUKU
detail: The room was cleaned neatly and the location is good with food options nearby and clubs close by. It's slightly away from the dangerous Kabukicho, which is nice because there aren't any drunk individuals or strange people nearby. The bed mattress was also very comfortable and nice. However, during my six-day stay, one day there was something that looked like blood on the bed sheets, which made me a bit uncomfortable, but I was too tired to do anything about it, so I'll take away one star. The rest was very friendly and nice.

name: APA Hotel Higashi-Nihonbashi-Ekimae
detail: I had work in Tokyo near Kyobashi (close to Hohmachi Station), but due to the forecast of heavy rain, I decided to stay overnight as I was concerned that the trains from Chiba might stop. Perhaps because it was Sunday, the location was great (just outside the station exit) and the price was reasonable, which was a relief. The surrounding area was quiet, and there was ice and a water dispenser on the second floor. The bathroom was slightly small, but the bed was comfortable, and I was able to relax without worry. I forgot to ask for a spoon when I went to the convenience store, so I inquired at the front desk, and they provided one immediately. I would like to use this place again if the opportunity arises.

name: APA Hotel Shibuya-Dogenzaka-Ue
detail: There were two adults with one double bed, and we were able to sleep well. There were several points that I thought were well thought out, and the creative solutions to ensure it didn't feel cramped in the limited space were great. The air conditioning adjustments were also possible. The TV was large compared to the size of the room, and there were various contents available, making one night feel insufficient. The check-out process was simply returning the card, which I thought was good because there was no waiting time. The breakfast was delicious, but the portion was a bit lacking. I think it would be nice if bread and coffee refills were available. The location is convenient, close to the busy area of Shibuya. Since I was able to book at a relatively low price, I think the cost performance was good. I would definitely like to use it again if I have the opportunity.
